submission.prose: Public entry point only: it wildcard-re-exports the merge API and its array helper. It implements no merge logic itself.
qualifications: Static reading of first-observed TypeScript sources; no runtime, packaging, tree-shaking, or mutation tests were performed.

children.prose: Implements rightward, recursive merging. `merge` folds inputs in order. Only plain incoming objects recurse; primitives, arrays, functions, dates, class instances, and other non-plain values replace the prior value. Each merged plain-object level is rebuilt, while untouched nested values can retain source references. Own string and symbol properties are considered; enumerability is preserved, other descriptor attributes are reset for non-enumerables, and `__proto__` is skipped. `mergeAndCompare` delegates every assigned incoming property to a caller callback after any nested recursion; `mergeAndConcat` supplies the array-concatenation callback. The exported `Merge` type approximates the folded result.

referent.description: runtime merge implementation and exported result type

qualifications: Behavior is inferred from source, not execution. Plain-object, array, and symbol classification is delegated to the external declaration-only `is-what` dependency, whose implementation was unavailable here.

The README claims new top-level objects, intact special instances, nested-reference retention, symbol/non-enumerable support, and overwrite/concat cases; these broadly match the implementation, but documentation remains an assertion.
